conclusion: Host checks passed offline: checks/gpu-mimus-layers.py covered the smaller-extent refusals and the default session's parity with mimus 9c57286b7 (refused jobs preserve job bytes, sequence and state), and apps/gpu-power-id/mimus-check.py executed the linked AArch64 caller against the platform and firmware model with cases for successful narrow and wide jobs, a missing tag, a wrong sum, a damaged guard and a missing timeline. The model reads the actual client commands, mappings and argument records and writes scalar integer results; the checks establish caller behavior with modeled hardware effects and do not execute USC instructions. apps/gpu-power-id/mimus-host-check.py used the preserved native-model log for parser and bundle checks and executed the actual returning runner entry with modeled transport for the default caller, accepted output and rejected output; rejection left completion false and transport failure false and reached the retention and quarantine handlers. The compiled submit path made ten comparisons before its first store, within the limit of twelve. These checks and the variant were removed with the application-specific session.
narrative: Workload: two jobs on one context, K = 512 and K = 516, each with 33 rows and 17 channels, four workgroups per job over padded rows and channels. Weights alternate between -128 and 127; activation rows alternate between 32,767 and -32,767; the second job produces positive and negative sums outside int32. 1,122 sums compared with scalar int64 products, 128 lane tags per job. Memory: 18 MiB returning reservation; 16 KiB weights, 128 KiB activations, 128 KiB output, 4 KiB job page, 8 KiB program pages; 71 GPU mappings of 4 KiB pages; about 360 KiB of retained backing for the context programs and arithmetic allocations. Session configuration accepted optional arena_bytes and output_bytes (zero selects 12 MiB and 2 MiB). Commands: build.py --fw-mimus --output IMAGE; mimus-check.py --image IMAGE/image.elf --output CHECK.
